cleanIntro: Ithaca's own Model 37 book, and it draws a line worth knowing before you start: for general cleaning only the barrel and the choke tube leave the gun. The fuller teardown — magazine cap, spring, follower, yoke and forend — is printed separately, and one line in the same book says some 37s have a barrel that is not meant to come off at all.

steps.title: Action open, chamber and magazine tube both checked
steps.action: With the safety on and the barrel pointed somewhere safe, press back on the action release and pull the forend fully to the rear. Then look and feel — in the chamber and in the magazine tube. A Model 37 loads and ejects through one port in the bottom of the receiver, so there is no side window to glance through and a shell held on the carrier is easy to miss by eye alone.
steps.aside: Check to make sure the gun is unloaded by looking and feeling in the chamber and magazine tube
steps.quote: Keeping the barrel pointed in a safe direction with the safety on, press back on the action release and pull the forend back to open the action
steps.cite: Model 37 Owners Manual — UNDATED — no edition or revision code is printed in the document — Care and Maintenance, Cleaning Instructions, step 1, p.5

steps.title: For a routine clean, only the barrel and choke leave the gun
steps.action: Decide how far you are going before you turn anything. Ithaca's cleaning section stops at the barrel and the choke tube — forend, magazine tube and slide all stay on the gun, and that is enough to clean a 37 after a day out. Take the fuller strip in the steps below only when you actually want the magazine tube and forend off.
steps.aside: All new Model 37’s will accept 2 3/4 or 3 shells.
steps.quote: only disassembly required for general cleaning is to remove the barrel and the choke tube.
steps.cite: Model 37 Owners Manual — UNDATED — no edition or revision code is printed in the document — Care and Maintenance, Cleaning Instructions, p.5

steps.title: Some 37s have a barrel that must not come off
steps.action: Check which gun you have before you rotate the barrel. Ithaca prints a carve-out in the same Care and Maintenance section: Model 37, DSII, DSIII, Home Defense and Turkeyslayer guns built with fixed barrels are not meant to have the barrel removed. If yours is a fixed-barrel gun, skip the barrel step entirely and clean the bore from the breech end with the barrel still on the receiver.
steps.quote: must be aware that the barrel is not intended to be removed.
steps.cite: Model 37 Owners Manual — UNDATED — no edition or revision code is printed in the document — Care and Maintenance, fixed-barrel note, p.4
steps.warn: This is a per-gun call the manual cannot make for you — the same five model names appear on both fixed-barrel and removable-barrel guns. If the barrel does not free itself after a quarter turn, stop rather than forcing it.

steps.title: Magazine nut backed off, barrel a quarter turn and straight out
steps.action: Hold the gun upright and back the magazine nut off until it sits snug against the magazine lug — the nut stays on the tube, it is only being freed from the barrel. Then rotate the barrel a quarter turn clockwise and draw it straight forward out of the receiver. Straight forward, not angled: the barrel lug runs in a slot and cocking it sideways binds it in place.
steps.aside: turn the barrel a 1/4 clockwise turn (Figure 14) and pull it straight out away from the receiver
steps.quote: turn the magazine nut counter clockwise until it is snug against the magazine lug
steps.cite: Model 37 Owners Manual — UNDATED — no edition or revision code is printed in the document — Disassembly, step 2, p.19
steps.warn: The book contradicts itself on this nut. Disassembly on p.19 says counter clockwise; Care and Maintenance on p.7 prints "turn the magazine nut clockwise until its snug against the magazine tube yoke" for the same operation. Both are Ithaca's words. Turn it whichever way loosens it on your gun and stop when it seats against the lug.

steps.title: Magazine cap unscrewed with your thumb on it
steps.action: The cap at the front of the magazine tube is holding the magazine spring compressed. Keep light pressure on it with your thumb the whole time you unscrew it, and let it up gradually once the threads run out. This is the step that fires a cap and a spring across a room if you let go halfway.
steps.quote: Grasp the magazine nut, turn it clockwise making sure you keep light pressure on the cap while unscrewing because it is spring loaded, until you completely remove it.
steps.cite: Model 37 Owners Manual — UNDATED — no edition or revision code is printed in the document — Disassembly, step 3, p.19
steps.warn: Do the whole step with the muzzle pointed away from your face. The spring behind the cap is long and it will travel.

steps.title: Magazine spring drawn out, not stretched out
steps.action: Ease the spring out of the tube rather than pulling it. A magazine spring that gets stretched or kinked during cleaning is the classic cause of a shotgun that will not feed the last shell afterwards, and the damage does not show until you are loading it.
steps.quote: Pull the spring gently out of the magazine tube being careful not to overstretch or bend the spring.
steps.cite: Model 37 Owners Manual — UNDATED — no edition or revision code is printed in the document — Disassembly, step 4, p.19

steps.title: Follower dropped into your hand
steps.action: Turn the gun upside down, free the red follower with a finger and catch it — cup your hand over the tube mouth first, because once it is loose it slides straight out. The follower is red for a reason: seeing it during unloading is how you know the tube is empty, so do not lose it.
steps.quote: place your hand over magazine tube to catch the follower; when inverted, the follower will slide into your hand
steps.cite: Model 37 Owners Manual — UNDATED — no edition or revision code is printed in the document — Disassembly, step 5, p.21

steps.title: Yoke screw out, yoke spread off the tube
steps.action: Take the small flathead screwdriver to the yoke screw at the end of the magazine tube and remove it. Then spread the yoke apart gently and slide it off the tube, and run the forend forward until the action locks. Spread it only as far as it needs — the yoke is a spring clip and over-opening it leaves it loose on reassembly.
steps.aside: Slide the forend forward until the action locks
steps.quote: remove the yoke screw located in the yoke at the end of the magazine tube
steps.cite: Model 37 Owners Manual — UNDATED — no edition or revision code is printed in the document — Disassembly, step 6, p.21

steps.title: Slide pin pushed across, forend off the tube
steps.action: Invert the gun and look up into the loading port for the slide pin. Push it across to the left with the same flathead screwdriver, then draw the forend off the front of the magazine tube. The pin is the only thing holding the slide assembly rod captive; if the forend will not come, the pin has not gone far enough over.
steps.quote: look into the load area and locate the slide pin the slide
steps.cite: Model 37 Owners Manual — UNDATED — no edition or revision code is printed in the document — Disassembly, step 8, p.21

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Barrel, magazine cap, spring, follower, yoke and forend are off the receiver. That is as far as Ithaca's book goes, and it says so in its own words. Everything from here is cleaning; the receiver internals, trigger housing and shell stops are not covered in these sixteen pages and are a service-department job.
steps.quote: No additional disassembly is required for cleaning.
steps.cite: Model 37 Owners Manual — UNDATED — no edition or revision code is printed in the document — Disassembly, Note, p.21

deepAbsentReason: Ithaca's Model 37 book stops at the forend. Its Disassembly section ends with a printed note that no additional disassembly is required for cleaning and that anything further goes to the Ithaca service department, and the General Cleaning Tips section sends further internal problems to a qualified gunsmith. There is no trigger-housing, bolt, carrier, shell-stop or ejector procedure anywhere in the sixteen pages, and there is no exploded view. No deeper procedure was invented from it.

cleaning.name: BORE & CHOKE
tasks: Feed the rod in from the breech end and push it through and out the muzzle — never start it at the muzzle
Work a solvent-wet patch the full length of the bore in both directions without reversing mid-bore
Dry-patch until the patch comes out clean, then run an oiled patch through to protect the bore
Take the choke tube out, clean its threads and the barrel's choke threads, and re-grease before refitting

cleaning.name: CHAMBER & THREADS
tasks: Wipe the inside of the chamber with a soft cloth and cleaning solvent
Scrub the barrel's threads and the receiver's internal threads with a soft bristle brush
Use a bristle brush on hard deposits, then re-run the wet, dry and oiled patches

cleaning.name: EXTERNAL METAL, TUBE & STOCK
tasks: Put a light coat of oil on all external metal parts to keep rust off
Wipe the magazine tube inside and out, and the follower and spring, before they go back
Wipe wood stocks and forends down with linseed oil
Leave camo-coated guns, synthetic stocks and synthetic forends out of the linseed step

reassembly: Slide the forend back onto the magazine tube with the slide assembly rod in line with the slot on the right side of the receiver.
Push the slide pin to the right only far enough to let the slide assembly rod pass it, then push the forend home until it clicks in.
Drop the follower into the tube tapered end down, fit the yoke with the pinch cut side up and aligned to the notch, and screw the yoke screw in without over-tightening it.
Slide the spring back into the tube without bending it, seat the magazine cap on the end of the spring and turn it until it rests against the yoke — do not cross-thread it.
Fit the barrel with its lug pointing left, turn it counter clockwise a quarter turn to line up with the dimple on the magazine cap, then snug the cap against the barrel lug until it clicks.
fncheck: With the gun confirmed empty, cycle the action several times and confirm the forend runs its full travel and locks up in battery, that the barrel is seated with no play, and that the safety moves through both positions. The manual's own last reassembly step is to cycle the action and make sure everything is in working order.
